messages:
nina: heads-up — hit a weird parity/dx bug in the JS starter: the SDK's schema-shim helper is coercing numeric strings to numbers when validating function outputs in JSON mode. in streaming cases this can lead to duplicated keys and a silently accepted payload that later breaks downstream workers. blocking a partner onboarding.

owen: ugh. can you paste a repro?

nina: repro (short):
1) starter app in JSON mode, function_call `lookup` expects {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"score\":{\"type\":\"number\"}}}
2) downstream tool streams tokens and emits `\"score\": \"42\"` in one chunk and later emits a final chunk `, \"score\": 42` (duplicate key due to streaming merge)
3) the JS helper coerces the first string to number, merges keys, validator accepts it, app sees inconsistent object (runtime libraries later pick the string or number unpredictably)

snippet sent to model:```json
{\"model\":\"gpt-js\",\"mode\":\"json\",\"function_call\":{\"name\":\"lookup\",\"arguments_schema\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"q\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}
```

logs:```
[2026-03-26T10:05:02Z] WARN shim: coercing string->number for key=score
[2026-03-26T10:05:02Z] INFO parser: saw duplicate key 'score' in streaming chunks, merging
[2026-03-26T10:05:02Z] INFO validator: validation passed after coercion
[2026-03-26T10:05:02Z] ERR downstream: worker json-decode failed - inconsistent types for key 'score'
```

tara: that's surprising. SDK shouldn't silently coerce in strict schema mode. we added the shim to help old noisy models, but it looks like streaming merges expose a hole.

nina: quick mitigation: set env var `REDWOOD_JS_SCHEMA_SHIM=false` in starter sample and restart; that causes the validator to fail-fast and surface the issue to the app instead of letting it through. partner unblocked.

owen: we should change the helper to 1) prefer fail-fast when duplicate keys are seen in streaming; 2) avoid coercion when streaming detected; 3) add a toggle `coerceOnFinalOnly` so older flows can opt-in.

tara: agreed. i'll open a small PR to the JS SDK to make coercion conditional on no-duplicates and to emit a clear validation error when duplicates are merged. also add an integration test in starter-samples that simulates split-token duplicates.

build-bot: CI: starter-samples/test-streaming failed on `js-duplicate-key-merge` (https://ci/c/13055) :red_circle:

own: thanks. nina, can you attach a tiny reproducer gist to the PR so support can reproduce locally? also let's add a short FAQ line in the starter-app README about streaming duplicate keys and the shim env var.

nina: will do. PR reference: https://repo/rw/js-sdk/pull/412 (shim guard + tests). starter-samples PR: https://repo/rw/starter-samples/pull/107 (env var + repro).

sam: tagging @security to confirm there are no parsing attack vectors here when we change merging semantics. we should be explicit in the docs about duplicate key handling.

tara: good call. i'll include a section in the PR description about the attack surface and recommended default (fail-fast).

own: plan: patch release for JS SDK once CI is green (24h). runtime should not change behavior now; prefer client-side guard. will follow up to sync parity across SDKs after JS patch.

nina: thanks everyone — partner unblocked with the env var workaround. i'll update the support ticket with steps and ETA. :thumbsup:
